title: Cycle Shape Declaration — Skipped Phases and Paused State
summary: `.rdd/cycle-status.md` gains two optional fields the Stop hook honors: `**Skipped phases:**`, a comma-separated list of phases the current cycle does not run, which the hook treats as having no required manifest artifacts; and `**Paused:**`, a dated line marking the cycle deliberately dormant, which short-circuits all per-phase manifest checks to allow. A new Pause Log section in cycle-status.md records each pause/resume event so the state stays visible rather than silent, preserving Invariant 8. The fields close a Stop-hook infinite-loop failure mode observed in Cycle 015 for mini-cycles (Mode D) and user-away sessions during an in-progress gate.
workflow_point: cycle-status.md schema, read by the Stop hook before phase-manifest dispatch
mechanism: Skipped phases / Paused declaration fields plus Pause Log audit trail

supersession.text: ADR-078 (Multi-Cycle Schema) folds this ADR's two header fields (`**Skipped phases:**`, `**Paused:**`) in as per-entry fields within a richer `## Cycle Stack` schema. The semantics established here remain current; the field placement migrates from per-file to per-entry. The rest of this ADR remains authoritative for the field semantics and hook behavior.

an indefinitely-paused cycle is a deliberately open state, not a closed one; this is distinct from Graduation (ADR-025), which formally closes a cycle
scoped cycles (ADR-026) and mini-cycles gain explicit structural support for skipped phases without requiring per-cycle hook configuration

the Stop hook (ADR-064) reads the new Skipped phases and Paused fields before dispatching to phase-manifest checks; the compound check and revision-aware re-audit reminder continue to fire for non-skipped, non-paused phases
post-migration enforcement-mode corpora get the skip/pause structural benefit, consistent with ADR-070's advisory-mode-vs-enforcement-mode migration boundary
